A_target.statement:
Let $p$ be a [[Definition:Prime Number|prime]].
Then:
:$\paren {p - 1}! \equiv -1 \pmod p$

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite [[Definition:Abelian Group|abelian group]].
Then the product of all elements of $G$ equals the product of its [[Definition:Self-Inverse Element|self-inverse elements]], since the other elements cancel in inverse pairs.

substitutions.self-inverse elements: solutions of x^2 = 1 mod p, namely 1 and -1

derived.non-self-inverse elements cancel in pair: all factors of (p-1)! pair off except 1 and p-1

validity_conditions: (Z/pZ)^* is abelian of order p-1; each element pairs with its distinct inverse except those equal to their own inverse.
x^2 = 1 mod p has exactly two solutions, 1 and p-1 = -1, since p is prime (a field).
So the product (p-1)! collapses to 1 * (-1) = -1 mod p.
proof_plan:
Work in $\paren {\Z / p \Z}^\times = \set {\eqclass 1 p, \ldots, \eqclass {p - 1} p}$.
The product of all its elements is $\paren {p - 1}! \bmod p$.

Pair each element with its [[Definition:Multiplicative Inverse|multiplicative inverse]].
Pairs of distinct elements multiply to $\eqclass 1 p$.

$x$ is self-inverse {{iff}} $x^2 = 1$, {{iff}} $\paren {x - 1} \paren {x + 1} = 0$.
As $\Z / p \Z$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]], the only solutions are $x = \pm 1$.
